solution:
The correct answer is the __**military strategy used by Babur**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Tulughama was a military tactic employed by Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India. 
 
• This strategy involved dividing his army into multiple units and using flanking maneuvers to encircle and attack the enemy from multiple directions. 
 
• This technique was effectively used in the Battle of Panipat (1526) and other battles to defeat larger armies.
 
• The term refers to a flanking and encirclement tactic that divided the army into three key parts:
 
• Central Force (Main Body): This group formed the core of the army and held the main battle line. It was tasked with engaging the enemy head-on.
 
• Flanking Forces (Left and Right Wings): These units were mobile and positioned to move swiftly around the enemy.
 
• Reserve Force (Ambushers): This group was hidden or positioned strategically to attack unexpectedly.
 
• The main idea was to simulate a retreat by certain parts of the army, luring the enemy into disarray.
 
• While the enemy pursued the "retreating" forces, the flanking units and reserves would close in, surround them, and attack from multiple directions.
